_comment: Cameras/sites that a human has VALIDATED against known-correct grades, and
which may therefore produce an auto-cleared (Tier A) case.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The classifier was trained and calibrated on a small
set of camera families. Measured on Messidor-2 (a manufacturer the model has
never seen): referable sensitivity falls from 95.0% in-domain to 75.2%, i.e.
roughly one referable patient in four is missed, while specificity holds.
Tier A is the only tier no human ever looks at, so that is exactly where an
unfamiliar camera does its damage -- silently. Source: Tanuj, ML Layer Final
Report 2026-09-21, section 3; the control was his request.
WHAT COUNTS AS VALIDATED. Someone compared this camera's output at this site
against known-correct grades and signed off. It is NOT 'this camera has been
used here a while' -- that is the separate camera/site probation check, which
counts cases and cannot tell a working camera from one the model is quietly
wrong about. Both run; they answer different questions.
A MISSING cameraDeviceId IS NOT VALIDATED. An unidentified camera is the one
we know least about. The probation check treats a missing id as cleared (a
blank field is a data-completeness problem, not evidence of a strange camera)
-- correct for that check, backwards for this one.
phcId '*' means 'validated for every site'. Use it only for a camera MODEL
validated across sites, never as a shortcut for an unvalidated one: it drops
the site half of the check, and site conditions (lighting, operator, mounting)
are part of what shifts the input distribution.
_enforceNote: false disables the Tier A floor entirely and logs once at startup. Intended
for local development against seed data, never for a deployment: with it off
an unvalidated camera can auto-clear again.

validated.validatedBy: DEMO SEED -- NOT A REAL VALIDATION
validated.note: Present so the demo corpus can still show a Tier A case. No clinical validation of this device has been performed at any site. Remove before any real deployment.
